title: The Longer Piece
problem: Break a unit-length stick at a point chosen uniformly along its length. What is the expected length of the longer piece?

hints.text: If the break point is X, the longer piece is max(X,1-X). Use symmetry around 1/2.
Double the integral of 1-X over X from 0 to 1/2.

solution.setup: Let X be the uniform break location. For X≤1/2, the longer piece has length 1-X; the other half is symmetric.
solution.sanityCheck: The longer piece is always between 1/2 and 1, so an expectation of 3/4 is plausible and is the midpoint of its uniform range.

keyInsight: Symmetry can reduce a piecewise continuous expectation to one simple integral.
recognitionCues: A uniformly random location and a max/min payoff suggest splitting at the symmetry point.
commonMistakes: Using the expected break point 1/2 as the expected longer length.
followUps: What is the expected length of the shorter piece?

source.notes: Original wording of a classic random-break problem.
